title: Kernel batching tactical briefing — Week of 2029-09-17
summary: Weekly tactical notes focused on kernel batching, KV cache behavior and a new experimental coalescer (mosaic). Contains experiment results, operational anomalies from Wed spike, and prioritized actions for next sprint.
meeting_notes:
Attendees: Priya (chair), Ethan, Li, Samira, oncall rotation (Jorge).

1) Quick status and context
- Rollout window: continuing gradual rollout of mosaic coalescer to 10% of traffic (canary). Observed early wins on throughput and a subtle p95 tail increase for short-seq chat workloads.
- Current mesh: legacy coalescer at 90% traffic, mosaic at 10%. Canary started 2029-09-13.
- Metrics snapshot (canary vs control, aggregated):
  * Tokens/s per GPU +12% (canary median)
  * Cost/unit (inference tokens) -8% (projected)
  * Latency p50 unchanged, p95 +18ms for sequences <128 tokens, p95 unchanged for longer sequences

2) Kernel-level observations
- Kernel handshake: slight increase in kernel-switch ops when mosaic tries to opportunistically coalesce micro-batches; appears to be due to extra quick-path checks. We traced hot call site to scheduler.c:enqueue_fast_path.
- Hypothesis: extra atomic CAS in fast-path is the dominant overhead for bursts <8 requests. We sketched an alternate fast-path (batched CAS) to amortize cost.
- Temporary mitigation: disable opportunistic micro-coalesce for sequences <32 tokens in mosaic. This cut the p95 delta by ~70% in the canary.

3) KV cache anomalies
- Observed KV cache duplication during a small-scale scheduler restart (2029-09-15 03:12 UTC). Two agents warmed same cache slots leading to transient memory pressure and one OOM in smoke cluster.
- Root cause: restart ordering race between cache manager and kernel affinity broker; cache manager reclaims slots after affinity broker already remapped slot ownership.
- Short-term fix: introduce a restart marker file and backoff 250ms for reclamation in the cache manager.
- Long-term: design change to slot ownership lease (proposal linked in JIRA-RT-8472).

4) Batching behavior and traffic shapes
- Traffic spike on Wed (unexpected marketing test) exposed the hopscotch that causes micro-batch splitting (lots of 1-2 token requests).
- Mosaic coalescer currently favors latency SLOs by windowing aggressively; suggested tweak: add an adaptive window that relaxes for observed high 1-token fractions to reduce split overhead.
- To test: run A/B where mosaic-adaptive-window uses history of last 60s 1-token ratio and scales coalesce window between 5ms-30ms.

5) Experiments and results
- Shadow A/B: shadowed control vs mosaic for ~72h across two clusters. Key findings: +9–14% throughput at similar median latency, but p95 regression concentrated on short conversations.
- Microbenchmark: batched CAS prototype reduced kernel handshake extra cost by ~40% in synthetic burst tests. Still needs integration.
- Cost sim: projected monthly savings for a p50 incremental traffic shift to mosaic ~6% infra spend.

6) Ops incident notes
- Incident at 2029-09-15 03:12 UTC (minor OOM): paged oncall, mitigation applied, no customer-visible errors. Postmortem: short blameless timeline will be created. Owner: Ethan.

7) Docs and rollout
- Playbook updates required: restart ordering, canary rollback checklist, and mosaic flags (ENV: MOSAIC_CANARY=1, MOSAIC_MIN_SEQ=32).
- Add a one-pager to Console explaining the canary behavior for platform SREs. Action: Samira to draft by 2029-09-20.

8) Misc notes from the room
- Li: noticed unusual GPU kernel occupancy patterns during low load; may tie to slot humidity (redistribution policy). Will run profiling with nvprof next week.
- Priya: request to add a simple metric exposing "micro-coalesce-events-per-second" for easier debugging in flight.
- Jorge (oncall): wants automated trigger to pause mosaic if p95 regression >25ms over baseline for 5m.

End of notes.
action_items: Ethan: own postmortem for 2029-09-15 OOM and link to JIRA-RT-8472 (due 2029-09-21)
Samira: draft canary one-pager for Console and SRE runbook (due 2029-09-20)
Li: run nvprof occupancy profile on two affected nodes and share flamegraphs (due 2029-09-22)
Priya: prototype batched-CAS fast-path and open PR to integrate (target 2029-09-25)
Oncall: add alert to pause mosaic canary when p95 delta >25ms sustained for 5m (owner Jorge, due 2029-09-19)
decisions: Pause opportunistic micro-coalesce for sequences <32 tokens in mosaic canary (effective immediately)
Implement restart marker + 250ms backoff in cache manager as interim mitigation for slot reclaim race
Proceed with A/B test for adaptive coalesce window using 60s 1-token ratio
open_questions: Is batched CAS safe across heterogeneous kernel versions? (compatibility matrix needed)
What guardrails should Console expose to teams before enabling mosaic internally?
Should we expand canary to 25% after next week's batched-CAS integration test?
retrospective: This week highlighted tradeoffs between raw throughput and short-tail latency. Mosaic looks promising for cost but needs a couple of kernel-level optimizations and clearer SRE guardrails before broader rollout. The team did well triaging the OOM and shipping a short-term fix quickly.
